extracted.intended_audience: poets, literary critics, and students of poetry/literary criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing, translating, and evaluating poetry: how a poet should choose diction, figures, metre, and imaginative procedure, and how critics should distinguish genuine poetic genius from affectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of grammar, logic, and psychology (Taste)
rubrics_metrics.description: By the principles of grammar, logic, psychology. In one word by such a knowledge of the facts, material and spiritual, that most appertain to his art ... becomes the representative and reward of our past conscious reasonings, insights, and conclusions, and acquires the name of Taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The poet should be grounded in grammar, logic, and an understanding of human psychology; this knowledge—applied with good sense and habit—constitutes Taste. Lack of such knowledge or its neglect would convict a writer of being 'no poet' but a vain or ignorant usurper. (Implicit scoring: mastery of these fundamentals distinguishes competent poetic practice from mere affectation.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Match linguistic register to the emotion or state
rubrics_metrics.description: By what rule ... is the latter to distinguish between the language suitable to suppressed, and the language, which is characteristic of indulged, anger? Or between that of rage and that of jealousy?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select vocabulary, syntax, and figures appropriate to the specific emotion or intensity being represented. The poet should distinguish subtle shades (suppressed vs indulged anger) rather than indiscriminately copying any angry speech; inappropriate register betrays inauthenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagination and meditation precede observation
rubrics_metrics.description: By meditation, rather than by observation? And by the latter in consequence only of the former?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetic insight should come from imaginative meditation which predisposes perception; mere literal copying of observed speech (e.g., collecting words from uncultivated society) is inferior. The poet's inner creative agency guides useful observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal rules of Imagination over external mechanical rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Could a rule be given from without, poetry would cease to be poetry, and sink into a mechanical art. The rules of the Imagination are themselves the very powers of growth and production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid imposing prescriptive external formulas that would make poetry mechanical. 'Rules' that are really the artist's imaginative powers cannot be fully expressed as external commandments; beware trying to reduce poetic creation to checklists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poet's intuitive discrimination between genuine and counterfeit
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the prerogative of poetic genius to distinguish by parental instinct its proper offspring from the changelings, which the gnomes of vanity or the fairies of fashion may have laid in its cradle or called by its names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop an intuitive critical sense (Taste) to separate authentic expressive choices from fashionable or vain artifices. Critics should respect this faculty in great poets and use it as a criterion of quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style must suit the compositional state
rubrics_metrics.description: Through the same process and by the same creative agency will the poet distinguish the degree and kind of the excitement produced by the very act of poetic composition. As intuitively will he know, what differences of style it at once inspires and justifies, what intermixture of conscious volition is natural to that state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose style, syntactic complexity, and rhetorical devices that are appropriate to the poet's mental state during composition; some levels of volition are natural and justified, others are not. Evaluate style relative to the compositional circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pseudo-poesy, affectation, and hysterical show
rubrics_metrics.description: As little difficulty do we find in excluding from the honors of unaffected warmth and elevation the madness prepense of pseudopoesy, or the startling hysteric of weakness over-exerting itself, which bursts on the unprepared reader in sundry odes and apostrophes to abstract terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-patterns include poems that simulate madness or excessive passion as a pose (e.g., Odes to Jealousy, to Hope). Such manufactured exuberance should be excluded from genuine poetic praise; prefer sincere emotion over theatrical excess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Juxtaposition and surprise must be rooted in imaginative vision, not mere artifice
rubrics_metrics.description: Such language and such combinations are the native produce neither of the fancy nor of the imagination; their operation consists in the excitement of surprise by the juxtaposition and apparent reconciliation of widely-different or incompatible things ... therefore, a species of art, a pure work of the skill, and implies a leisure and self-possession incompatible with the steady terror of a mind possessed and filled with the grandeur of its subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using striking contrasts or reconciliations, ensure they arise from a genuine imaginative synthesis (sympathy, inward vision). If juxtaposition is merely an intellectual trick or a product of leisure-bound artifice, it will feel false, especially where overwhelming subject-matter calls for sustained passion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condemnation of non-conversational diction requires substantive fault
rubrics_metrics.description: When a poem ... is evidently vicious in the figures and contexture of the whole, yet for the condemnation of which no reason can be assigned, except that it differs from the style in which men actually converse, then, and not till then, can I hold this theory to be either plausible or practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reject a poetic style merely because it diverges from ordinary conversation. Only when figures, constructions, or contexture are truly vicious (i.e., defective in sense, coherence, or truth to things) should style be condemned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apt expression of thought while preserving rhyme and metre
rubrics_metrics.description: The talent ... required in order to make excellent verses ... the talent to seek only the apt expression of the thought, and yet to find at the same time with it the rhyme and the metre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuate skill in reconciling natural expression with formal constraints. Praise works (e.g., Gellert, certain English poets) that express thought exactly as one would speak while remaining dignified and metrically correct; undue contortions to fit rhyme/metre are faults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural diction that could exist in conversation yet remains dignified
rubrics_metrics.description: It was a strange and curious phenomenon ... to read verses in which everything was expressed just as one would wish to talk, and yet all dignified, attractive, and interesting; and all at the same time perfectly correct as to the measure of the syllables and the rhyme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for language that feels immediately natural and conversational without losing the dignity and heightened interest of poetry. This balance is a mark of excellence and popular appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid ornamental artifices lacking necessity
rubrics_metrics.description: In what instances such figures and colors of speech degenerate into mere creatures of an arbitrary purpose, cold technical artifices of ornament or connexion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures of speech and decorative devices must be justified by the poem's imaginative truth; if they exist only as ornament for its own sake, they are decadent. Detect and penalize ornament that does not arise organically from subject or feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use authoritative exemplars across ages and countries to confirm principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirmed by the authority of works whose name is not of one country nor of one age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When establishing principles of poetic taste and style, appeal to exemplary works from diverse traditions and times. Cross-cultural/historical exemplars serve as confirmation that principles are rooted in enduring poetic practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be wary of forced archaisms and translator's mannerisms
rubrics_metrics.description: It strikes me as a fault in his version, that it brings the lyric flow of the Allegro, Penseroso, and Lycidas, so strongly to mind, that we seem to be reading Milton instead of Pindar ... Cary's Dante, on the other hand, is a noble poem, that may be read and admired apart from the Italian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In translation, avoid imposing the translator's familiar idiom or national manner onto the original poet; this can mask the original. Sometimes a prose translation better exhibits the original's force than strained metrical imitation (example: Pindar).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prose translation can better represent certain originals than metrical versions
rubrics_metrics.description: A prose translation, like that of the Psalms and Prophets, would exhibit more of Pindar to the English reader, or would, at least, disguise him less than any metrical version ... whose metre is so irrepressible in a modern tongue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an original's metre and metaphor are unrepresentable, prefer plain prose translation to capture sense and bold imagery rather than awkward metrical pastiche. Evaluate translations on how well they communicate the original's ideas and images, not on their imitation of form alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject rhetorical caprices that lack inward vision
rubrics_metrics.description: Are such rhetorical caprices condemnable only for their deviation from the language of real life? ... Surely good sense, and a moderate insight into the constitution of the human mind, would be amply sufficient to prove, that such language and such combinations are the native produce neither of the fancy nor of the imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique poems that rely on flashy rhetorical devices without an underlying imaginative root. Rhetorical caprice that merely delights by novelty or extravagant phrase but has no coherent imaginative basis should be judged harshly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticism should establish principles of writing rather than merely rules for judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: The ultimate end of criticism is much more to establish the principles of writing, than to furnish rules how to pass judgment on what has been written by others; if indeed it were possible that the two could be separated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical evaluation should aim to articulate underlying principles (taste, imaginative procedure, truth to human nature) that guide writing, not only to create checklists for verdicts. Use criticism pedagogically to improve practice, not merely to condemn.
